_status: Module 4, Lesson 4.1 'The endpoint baseline' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): its eight controls grouped by the memory phrase Update, protect, encrypt, lock. Which control stops which everyday attack is a teaching simplification, not a measurement. Fictional office.

attacks.label: Old browser weakness used by a web page
Malware tries to install itself as administrator
A device on the café Wi-Fi probes the laptop
An unknown USB stick from the car park
Field laptop stolen from a car
Old work phone sold without a wipe
A visitor uses a PC left unlocked
A phone left on a jeepney seat

scenes.title: No baseline
scenes.text: Ten everyday things that happen to work devices. With no baseline, every one of them lands.

scenes.title: Update
scenes.text: Security updates installed promptly, automatically where possible, and unused features and accounts turned off.

scenes.title: Protect
scenes.text: Endpoint protection running and current, the device's own firewall on, daily work as a standard user, and only approved, encrypted USB drives.

scenes.title: Encrypt
scenes.text: Full-disk encryption: a lost or stolen device does not mean lost data.

scenes.title: Lock
scenes.text: The screen locks after a few idle minutes, and a PIN or password reopens it. Update, protect, encrypt, lock: nothing lands.
